Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied algebra and scheme results. For every DVR R, Rsh is a faithfully flat DVR with the same uniformizer and separably closed residue field; it is the filtered colimit of local etale R-algebras. Smooth schemes over a strictly henselian local ring lift rational special-fibre points to sections; those special points are dense. Complete proof strategy: Fix a separable closure ks of k. Use pointed local etale R-algebras with residue embeddings into ks; their fibre products and the chosen residue point make a directed system. Each such local algebra is flat over R; its maximal ideal is generated by pi, because its residue fibre is a separable field. Its local ring is regular of dimension one, hence a DVR. The transition maps are injective local maps and preserve pi. In the union Rsh, every nonzero element is pi to an integer power times a unit, as already true at a finite stage. Every nonzero ideal has a least such power, so is principal. Thus the union itself is a Noetherian DVR, without excellence. The union embeds in the chosen separable closure of K and is R-torsion-free, hence R-flat by the published PID criterion. Since the extension is local with the same nonzero residue fibre it is faithfully flat by the published criterion. Its residue field is ks. The etale-local universal property and henselian lifting follow directly: an etale neighbourhood and residue point involve finitely many coefficients and descend to a finite stage; adjoining that pointed neighbourhood to the directed system supplies its section in the limit. Consequently the union is strictly henselian.

For smooth V/Rsh and a special ks-point, choose differential coordinates at the point. Cutting out the coordinate differences gives an etale slice through it, with unchanged residue field (BLR 2.2/14, whose proof was read). The defining henselian property gives a section of that slice, and hence a section of V. Every nonempty smooth finite-type open over the separably closed field has a rational point by the exact published `lem-nonempty-smooth-scheme-finite-separable-point`; therefore these section specializations are dense. For the generic fibre of a smooth integral model, a dense generic open also contains a section: the complement closure is horizontal and cannot contain a special-fibre component, so a special section outside that closure works. Equivalently one can use the relative dimension upper semicontinuity supplier below. This also proves the DVR specialization of BLR 5.3/7 needed in finite translate enlargement.

operations.before: Let $A\to S$ and $B\to S$ be abelian schemes of relative dimensions $g_A,g_B$ and let $S'\to S$ be a morphism. Then the base change $A_{S'}=A\times_SS'\to S'$ is an abelian scheme of relative dimension $g_A$, its $S'$-group structure is induced by that of $A$, and for every $s'\in S'$ with image $s\in S$ the fibre $(A_{S'})_{s'}$ is the base change $A_s\times_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(s')$ of abelian varieties. Likewise $A\times_SB\to S$ is an abelian scheme of relative dimension $g_A+g_B$ with the product group law. Kernels commute with arbitrary base change by their fibre-product definition; the base change of a finite locally free subgroup scheme is again such a subgroup, with the same rank. Scheme-theoretic images are not asserted to commute with arbitrary base change. The structural properties of an abelian scheme and geometric connectedness of fibres are preserved by base change; products have smooth proper geometrically connected fibres and the sum of the dimensions.

Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied scheme and cohomology results. For projective geometrically integral A/k, sufficiently positive relative effective Cartier divisors with fixed Hilbert polynomial form a finite-type open Hilbert chart D. Its class map to the rigidified Picard sheaf is relatively a smooth projective-space bundle over the appropriate open positive-class subfunctor, on arbitrary tests. The diagonal of that sheaf is represented and separated; after representability the Picard scheme is separated. Complete proof strategy: Fix a very ample line bundle H on A. The relative effective-divisor functor is an open of the published Hilbert scheme: on a flat finitely presented family, being cut out by a fibrewise regular element with invertible ideal is open, by the local flatness criterion plus Nakayama and proper projection of the bad locus. For a fixed Hilbert polynomial, this divisor scheme D is finite type and quasi-projective. Use positive charts with a specified Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity bound: impose the finitely many higher-cohomology vanishings in that regularity definition, using the universal finite cohomology complex. The published relative-regularity/base-change supplier propagates these finitely many vanishings to all required nonnegative twists. After twisting by a sufficiently high H power every individual test family is locally on its base in such a chart, by Serre vanishing. The chosen chart is an open D^+, with fixed polynomial and fixed finite regularity conditions; do not define openness by an unproved infinite intersection of vanishings. A line bundle satisfying these conditions has finite locally free sections, compatible with every base change, with positive rank.

 The map D^+ to the line-bundle sheaf is relatively represented by projective spaces: for an arbitrary test family L, divisors with class L are fibrewise nonzero sections up to units from the test base. Integral fibres make every nonzero fibre section regular. Hence the fibre is P((p_*L)^∨), scheme theoretically, and is smooth projective surjective. The linear-equivalence relation R on D^+ is therefore a represented smooth projective relation, of finite type, with both projections flat. Its map to D^+×D^+ is a monomorphism. The source is separated and finite type, so the published generic quotient theorem applies exactly, yielding a nonempty saturated open W and Y=W/R_W.

 Separatedness can be checked on these locally finite-type charts. If a rigidified line bundle on A_R, for a DVR R over the field, is trivial generically, its Cartier divisor is supported on the irreducible special fibre of the smooth regular A_R. On a regular scheme Cartier and Weil divisors agree, and this divisor is an integer multiple of the special fibre, the principal divisor of the uniformizer. Thus its class is trivial modulo a base line bundle. For diagonal representability and quasi-compactness, on the Noetherian product T of two finite-type divisor charts put M=L1^−1⊗L2 with the prescribed rigidification. A universal finite free cohomology complex has H0(M_T′)=ker(d0:K0⊗OT′→K1⊗OT′) on every test. Evaluation at the unit is a linear functional on this kernel; choosing a free representative of the degree-zero evaluation chain map gives its linear extension to K0. Sections with d0(s)=0 and e(s)=1 are therefore represented by a closed subscheme of the finite-rank affine vector bundle K0, defined by finitely many linear equations. Restrict to the open where the section is invertible everywhere on A: the zero locus of the universal section is closed, and its proper image in the parameter scheme is closed. This open is Noetherian, finite type, and quasi-compact. Such sections are exactly rigidified isomorphisms L1→L2, uniquely if they exist. Thus the diagonal is representable and quasi-compact on these covering chart products. The Noetherian DVR valuative uniqueness criterion now gives separatedness. Chain evaluation can be constructed by an affine Čech model and transferred to the finite projective complex; this should be written explicitly in authoring.

 The universal Hilbert ideal is flat over its Noetherian chart base because both the structure sheaf and universal flat quotient are base-flat. On a fibre where the ideal is a line bundle, the Noetherian fibrewise-flatness criterion makes it flat over the target local ring, and the finite-flat local freeness criterion makes it rank one. The locus is open; proper projection of its failure gives the divisor open in the Hilbert chart. Arbitrary test families descend locally to finitely generated k-algebras by finite-presentation spreading of the line bundle and its inverse, so these representing opens and linear-system universal properties apply to every test.

For general projective geometrically integral A, the Picard fppf sheaf is the sheafification of T↦Pic(A_T)/p_T^*Pic(T). Rigidification is used only after a rational section e is supplied; normalization then identifies this sheaf with e-rigidified classes. A finite separable extension supplies a rational point of the smooth locus when needed, and the affine diagonal descends by affine algebra descent. The separatedness proof uses inverse sections and the integral special fibre, so it does not require A to be smooth or regular.

operations.before: Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied algebra and scheme results. Let R be a DVR, K its fraction field, k its residue field, and Rsh a chosen strict henselization. In clauses involving A, let A/K be the given abelian variety. For a strict law over a strictly henselian DVR, finitely many section translates yield Y on which original X times X multiplication is everywhere defined. Y becomes a smooth separated finite-type group scheme containing X as fibre-dense open; any two group completions of a birational law are canonically isomorphic. Complete proof strategy: The multiplication graph domains Qn form increasing opens of the fixed Noetherian X times X, so stabilize. If a section translation still fails, glue its translate and strictly increase Qn, contradiction. Sections meet all dense opens in either fibre: for the generic fibre, specialize its excluded closed set and use dimension/flatness to leave a dense special open. Factor multiplication near any pair through a suitable such section. Source locators: BLR 5.3/6–7 specialized to DVR; BLR 5.3/8; 5.1/3–4. For generic auxiliary a express bc=(ba)(a inverse c); strict graph calculus puts the two factors in original X on a dense faithfully flat cover, and global X times X multiplication makes the law defined there. Descend its domain. Repeat for left division; the representable subgroup of birational maps supplies unit and inverse. Uniqueness uses the smooth surjection X times X to each completion and morphism descent. Source locators: BLR 5.3/6–7 specialized to DVR; BLR 5.3/8; 5.1/3–4.

Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied scheme and cohomology results. For any field k and any symmetric lambda:A→A^vee, there is a finite separable extension k'/k and a line bundle L on A_{k'} with lambda_{k'}=phi_L. In particular this holds over every separably closed field, including characteristic two. Complete proof strategy: 

For λ:A→B, set M=(id,λ)^*P. Biextension identities give φ_M=λ+λ^∨. If λ is symmetric, N=M² has φ_N=4λ. Thus A[4]⊂K(N). The theta commutator e_N on A[4] has values in μ4, and e_N(2y,2z)=e_N(y,z)^4=1. Since [2]:A[4]→A[2] is fppf onto, A[2] is isotropic scheme theoretically even in characteristic 2.

Here is a local replacement for EGM's deferred Ext(H,Gm)=0 fact, once finite Cartier exactness is proved. Let 0→Gm→E→H→0 be a commutative extension over an algebraically closed field and n annihilate H. Then [n]:E→Gm restricts to the nth-power map on Gm, and F=E[n]→H is a finite μn-torsor. Cartier exactness makes F^D→(μn)^D=Z/n fppf onto. A nonempty finite scheme over an algebraically closed field has a rational point, so choose χ:F→Gm restricting to the tautological μn character. The map Gm×F→E, (t,h)↦th, is a μn-torsor; (t,h)↦tχ(h) is invariant under its kernel and descends to a retraction E→Gm. Its kernel maps isomorphically to H, so the extension splits. Applying this to the theta extension over an isotropic subgroup supplies a linearization, and ordinary flat descent gives N=[2]^*L. Then 4λ=4φ_L and cancellation through the fppf epimorphism [4] gives λ=φ_L.

 To represent the locus where the universal defect A×S→A^vee equals zero, pull back the finitely presented ideal of the unit. On a finite-type affine chart of S choose a sufficiently large projective twist of this coherent ideal and finitely many global generators, producing O_A(-n)^m→I. This presentation remains surjective after every test-base change. Its composite to O_A is a list of sections of O_A(n); their coefficient vectors lie in the finite locally free constant-family module H^0(A,O_A(n))⊗O_S. Vanishing of those finitely many coefficients represents the locus on all tests. These closed loci glue independently of the chosen twist. The equality locus is a torsor under B=ker(phi) from the preceding homogeneous-bundle result, so it becomes B after an algebraically closed realization and is smooth over k. The published finite-separable-point theorem then supplies a realization over a finite separable extension.

 To represent the realizing-bundle torsor over k, spread the realizing line bundle and equality from the algebraic closure to a finite field extension K/k. Over K it is represented by A^vee_K using the Poincare bundle and all-test kernel equality. The canonical finite-field descent datum is effective because this projective representative has affine-contained finite descent orbits; Serre vanishing supplies the required affine opens. The descended torsor is nonempty smooth finite type, so a finite separable point realizes lambda. This does not assume representability of the full Picard scheme over k.
